finding.claim: The purge handler calls checkPerm(u, "admin") but discards the boolean result, so the admin check is never enforced. Any caller who reaches the route can run purgeAll(). The sibling rotateKeys handler enforces the check correctly with mustPerm.
finding.source: Any authenticated (or otherwise able-to-reach-route) non-admin user sending an HTTP request to the purge handler. Their User comes from the request context via userFrom.
finding.sink: purgeAll() at handlers.go:27, a destructive admin-only operation.

trace.note: u := userFrom(r) loads the caller's User from the request context
checkPerm(u, "admin") returns a bool that is ignored, with no if/return/throw

finding.guards_checked: Compared with rotateKeys (handlers.go:33), which checks the mustPerm result and returns on failure. checkPerm itself writes no error response. Only handlers.go exists in the directory, so no router or middleware that might add an admin guard is visible. I could not check the route registration, so it is an assumption that no upstream guard exists.

verdict.guard_found: none in handlers.go (checkPerm at line 12 returns a bool with no side effects; its result is discarded at line 26). Router and middleware are not visible in the directory.
verdict.reason: handlers.go:26 calls checkPerm(u, "admin") as a bare statement, so the bool result is dropped and purgeAll() at handlers.go:27 runs for any caller who reaches the route, while rotateKeys at handlers.go:33 correctly tests mustPerm. Any upstream admin middleware cannot be ruled out, since only this file exists.
